candidates.title: VoLLM: Smoothness-aware Serving of LLM-powered Voice Q&A via Adaptive Preemption
candidates.venue: IEEE International Parallel and Distributed Processing Symposium
candidates.abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) are increasingly deployed for voice Q&A, mainstream serving frameworks over-look inter-token latency, which is crucial for natural, real-time speech fluency. Current frameworks, optimized for end-to-end metrics, further struggle due to the monolithic co-batching of speech and LLM modules, preventing module-wise tuning under heterogeneous computational profiles and causing severe smoothness degradation under high concurrency. We introduce VoLLM, a smoothness-aware serving framework designed for SpeechLLMs. VoLLM’s core contributions are: (i) an offline latency-bounded sampling profiler that reduces sampling space for efficient latency modeling; (ii) an online time-budget-aware adaptive preemption scheduler that adaptively inserts new requests while preserving inter-token constraint for ongoing requests; and (iii) a stateful batch executor that enables module-wise batch inference based on request status. VoLLM achieves up to a 92.7% reduction in average response latency across diverse NVIDIA GPUs while guaranteeing fluent token emission.
candidates.reason: VoLLMは音声対話LLMのトークン間遅延と発話の滑らかさを重視したサービング。オフライン遅延上限制約プロファイラ、オンライン時間予算適応プリエンプション、音声・LLMモジュール別の状態付きバッチ実行を組み合わせる。IEEE Computer Societyの原著要旨は複数NVIDIA GPUで平均応答遅延を最大92.7%削減し流暢な出力を保証すると報告。

candidates.title: Dynamic Hot Expert Replication with Load and Topology-Aware Joint Gating for Distributed MoE Inference
candidates.venue: International Workshop on Quality of Service
candidates.abstract: Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models enable efficient scaling of large language models via sparse expert activation. However, their inference latency and throughput in distributed settings are often constrained by expert load imbalance and communication overhead, especially in online inference with dynamic and non-stationary request patterns. Imbalanced expert popularity leads to hot experts, which degrades tail latency. Although replicating hot experts is an effective strategy to mitigate expert load imbalance, existing expert replication-based MoE inference systems often rely on noisy load signals and overlook communication topology, limiting their adaptability to rapidly changing workloads. To overcome these limitations, we propose DETAG, a distributed MoE inference system that combines dynamic hot expert replication with load- and topologyaware joint gating. Specifically, DETAG introduces a lightweight dynamic hot expert pool, enabling on-demand expert replication to improve expert load balance and reduce communication overhead. In addition, DETAG further incorporates an Exponential Moving Average (EMA) smoothed, load- and topologyaware joint gating mechanism that incorporates both smoothed expert load and communication cost into routing decisions. Experiments on multi-node GPU clusters with representative MoE models show that DETAG significantly reduces cross-node communication, improves expert load balance, and achieves up to 2.54× speedup over existing MoE inference systems.
candidates.reason: DETAGは分散MoE推論におけるホットexpertの負荷偏りとノード間通信を抑える。必要に応じ複製する動的ホットexpertプールと、EMA平滑化負荷・通信トポロジー費用を同時考慮するjoint gatingを導入。複数GPUノードで既存MoE推論方式比最大2.54倍の高速化を報告。

candidates.title: SEC: Enabling MLLMs for Low-Latency IoT Video Analysis via Semantic-Aware Edge–Cloud Collaboration
candidates.abstract: The rapid proliferation of Internet of Things (IoT)-enabled cameras has driven increasing demand for low-latency, intelligent video understanding in real-world applications such as smart cities and industrial automation. While multimodal large language models (MLLMs) offer unprecedented capabilities in semantic reasoning and natural language-based video comprehension, their deployment in latency-sensitive IoT environments remains challenging due to high computational costs and sequential decoding bottlenecks. Moreover, conventional edge–cloud video analysis frameworks often rely on semantic-agnostic frame sampling, leading to information loss or redundant data transmission. In this article, we propose <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$SEC$ </tex-math></inline-formula>, a semantic-aware edge–cloud collaborative framework for efficient and accurate video analysis. <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$SEC$ </tex-math></inline-formula> introduces a task-aware key frame selection mechanism at the edge to maximize semantic relevance while minimizing bandwidth usage and a novel adaptive speculative decoding (SPD) framework with tree-based parallel generation on the cloud to accelerate MLLM inference. Extensive experiments under realistic edge–cloud deployment settings on four video understanding benchmarks demonstrate that the proposed <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$SEC$ </tex-math></inline-formula> framework achieves superior performance, significantly reducing the end-to-end inference latency while improving the accuracy, a rare win-win in latency-critical IoT systems.
candidates.reason: SECはIoT動画のMLLM推論を対象に、エッジ側でタスクに応じた意味的キーフレーム選択を行って通信量を削減し、クラウド側で木構造の適応的投機デコードにより生成を並列化する。4種の動画理解ベンチマークで実配備を想定したエンドツーエンド遅延低下と精度改善を報告。マルチモーダル推論システムに直接関連。
